description: Cost behaviour both engines must share: `kdb_id = c` and `kdb_id IN (...)` are resolved by key (never a scan), rowBudget bounds rows EXAMINED (not returned), and a result bound never truncates the scan. Read by go/kdb/sql/cost_behaviour_fixture_test.go and kdb-sql's jvmTest CostBehaviourFixtureTest.
id: document i (0-based) has id 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<i+1, 12 digits>; ${id:N} in sql/params means the id of the document with 1-based number N

cases.name: equality on kdb_id is a key lookup, not a scan
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = '${id:3}'

cases.name: reversed operands
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE '${id:3}' = kdb_id

cases.name: bound parameter
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = ?

cases.name: IN list; the unknown id contributes nothing
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id IN ('${id:3}', '${id:1}', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000999') ORDER BY name

cases.name: the rest of the WHERE still applies (match)
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = '${id:3}' AND rank = 2

cases.name: the rest of the WHERE still applies (no match)
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = '${id:3}' AND rank = 9

cases.name: a string that is not a uuid names nothing
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = 'not-a-uuid'

cases.name: IN of strings that are not uuids
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id IN ('x', 'y')

cases.name: key lookup past a tiny maxRows
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = '${id:50}'

cases.name: <> on kdb_id is a scan
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE kdb_id <> '${id:3}'

cases.name: OR with a key is a scan that sees both sides
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE kdb_id = '${id:3}' OR rank = 7 ORDER BY name

cases.name: LIKE on kdb_id is a scan
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE kdb_id LIKE '%0001'

cases.name: a scan over more rows than the budget is aborted
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE rank >= 0 ORDER BY name LIMIT 1

cases.name: the budget counts rows examined, not rows returned (selective filter)
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE name = 'n049'

cases.name: a budget equal to the namespace size is enough
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE name = 'n049'

cases.name: an aggregate that reads everything is bounded too
the result bound does not limit the scan: filtered count past maxRows
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE rank >= 10
